prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S031: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is referred to by the site engineering alias Kestrel in drawings and maintenance records for this deployment.
S032: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is located on a graded pad near the central ridge road so that launch, recovery, charging, and shelter functions remain accessible to maintenance personnel.
S033: The dock includes weather-rated enclosures, charging interfaces, local health monitoring, and a secure network termination for coordination with the rest of the support system.
S034: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock produces the Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records that a flight battery has reached the configured replacement threshold.
S035: Drone Tasking Service manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, and presents task status without acting as an independent authority for flight release.
S036: The Drone Pilot Operator uses Drone Tasking Service to review proposed routes, current dock status, and operational constraints before coordinating any field action through established procedures.
S037: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine is referred to by the site engineering alias Lantern in architecture diagrams and configuration work orders.
S038: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine aggregates camera detections, weather inputs, geospatial context, and operator feedback into traceable recommendations for fire detection and suppression support.
S039: Smoke Classifier Module runs as a bounded analytics component that scores visual observations for plume likelihood and passes confidence values to the broader analytics workflow.
S040: The analytics services retain event timing, source identifiers, model version information, and operator acknowledgments so that later review can reconstruct how a recommendation was presented.
S041: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node is referred to by the site engineering alias Brindle in network inventory and integration test records.
S042: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and configured quality checks to provide a consistent weather picture for the operating area.
S043: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node sends the Wind Shift Bulletin when its configured weather rules identify a significant change in local wind behavior.
S044: VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides a monitored bridge between selected radio traffic and operator workstations, with recording and access controls aligned to incident policy.
S045: Caldera Incident Command Portal is the primary operator interface for the Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, and other command staff who need consolidated situational information.
S046: The portal displays camera views, detection history, weather context, map layers, and status transitions such as Confirmed Ignition State and Airspace Restricted State.
S047: Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console supports the Air Attack Supervisor and Tanker Base Manager by presenting aircraft coordination data, loading status, and mission notes relevant to suppression support.
S048: East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump are represented in the site layout as monitored ground assets whose readiness and fault indications are visible to authorized operations staff.
S049: Crewline Mobile Tablet provides the Helitack Crew Leader with field access to assigned incident context, map references, and updates that have been approved for mobile distribution.
S050: Across the site, network segmentation, time synchronization, equipment health checks, and audit logging are treated as baseline infrastructure rather than optional add-ons.
S051: The detection workflow begins when the North Lookout Camera Mast, South Lookout Camera Mast, or Horizon Ridge Drone Dock provides an observation that may indicate a new ignition.
S052: Each observation is time stamped, georeferenced, and associated with equipment status before it is evaluated as operational evidence.
S053: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine receives the observation context and normalizes image, thermal, and weather attributes into a common event record.
S054: Smoke indications are initially assessed for plume texture, persistence, motion, and contrast against the background terrain.
S055: Thermal cues are treated as supporting evidence unless they persist across sequential frames or align with a visible smoke indication.
S056: The Smoke Classifier Module produces the Ridge Shadow Mask when terrain-shadow conditions could otherwise inflate a smoke confidence score.
S057: The analytics score is not considered a declaration of fire, because atmospheric glare, dust, vehicle exhaust, and cloud shadow can produce similar signatures.
S058: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides local wind, humidity, temperature, and stability context that helps determine whether an indication is plausible for active combustion.
S059: When the automated confidence level exceeds the screening threshold, the Caldera Incident Command Portal opens a triage case for human review.
S060: The Duty Detection Officer reviews the triage case, compares current imagery with recent frames, and checks whether the indication is growing, drifting, or disappearing.
S061: The Duty Detection Officer may request a fresh pan, tilt, or zoom view from the nearest fixed camera when the initial frame is ambiguous.
S062: If terrain, smoke column height, or occlusion prevents a clear fixed-camera view, the Drone Tasking Service may prepare a verification task for the Horizon Ridge Drone Dock.
S063: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed verification task is safe for launch conditions and consistent with current operating constraints.
